text: Fill in the missing term in each sentence about cytochrome P450.
questions: Cytochrome P450 is classified as a *monooxygenase/mixed-function oxidase/mixed function oxidase:How many of the two oxygen atoms end up in the substrate?* because it inserts one atom of oxygen into the substrate while the other atom forms water.
The cytochrome P450 reaction requires electrons from *NADPH:Which reduced coenzyme supplies the reducing equivalents?*, which are delivered by a flavoprotein reductase containing FAD and FMN.

Drug-metabolising CYP450 enzymes reside in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum and are therefore called *microsomal:What name is given to enzymes from the microsome fraction on differential centrifugation?* enzymes.

The characteristic absorbance peak used to name cytochrome P450 is measured with the reduced enzyme bound to *carbon monoxide:This gas is bound to the reduced haem iron for the spectral measurement.*.

overallFeedback.feedback: CYP450 is a monooxygenase using NADPH electrons to hydroxylate substrates; its location in the smooth ER (the microsomal fraction) and its characteristic 450 nm CO-absorbance peak are defining features that explain how inducers and inhibitors alter drug clearance.
